introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section 1 is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section 2 in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section 2 answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark(s) for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State Hooke's Law. *[2 marks]*

In order to determine whether a certain spiral spring obeys Hooke's Law or not, a student conducted an experiment and obtained the following readings.

| Force applied /N | 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Extension /cm | 0 | 18 | 35 | 54 | 70 | 90 |

(ii) Plot a graph of force applied (y-axis) against extension (x-axis). *[6 marks]*

(iii) Determine the gradient of your graph. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Hooke's law:** the extension of a spring (or of an elastic material) is **directly proportional to the force (load) applied to it**, provided the **elastic limit** is not exceeded ($F = ke$).

(ii) **Graph to plot (described).** Axes: extension $e$/cm on the x-axis (scale $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ to $10\,\mathrm{cm}$, from 0 to 90) and force $F$/N on the y-axis (scale $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ to $1\,\mathrm{N}$, from 0 to 10), both labelled with their units. Plot the six points $(e, F)$: $(0, 0)$, $(18, 2)$, $(35, 4)$, $(54, 6)$, $(70, 8)$, $(90, 10)$. Draw the **best straight line through the origin**, with the points scattered evenly on both sides of it. The points lie very close to a straight line through the origin, because $F/e$ stays almost constant ($0.111$ to $0.114\,\mathrm{N\,cm^{-1}}$).

(iii) Take a large triangle on the line, for example between $(0, 0)$ and $(90, 10)$:

$$\text{gradient} = \dfrac{\Delta F}{\Delta e} = \dfrac{10 - 0}{90 - 0} = 0.11\,\mathrm{N\,cm^{-1}}$$

that is **$0.11\,\mathrm{N\,cm^{-1}} = 11\,\mathrm{N\,m^{-1}}$**. This gradient is the **force constant (spring constant) $k$** of the spring. Because the graph is a straight line through the origin, **the spring obeys Hooke's law** over this range of forces.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define pressure. *[2 marks]*

(ii) State two factors that affect the pressure exerted by a solid on a surface. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Pressure** is the **force acting normally (perpendicularly) per unit area** of a surface: $P = \dfrac{F}{A}$. Its SI unit is the pascal ($1\,\mathrm{Pa} = 1\,\mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}$).

(ii) Since $P = F/A$, the pressure exerted by a solid depends on: (1) the **force (weight) pressing normally on the surface**: a larger force gives a larger pressure; (2) the **area of contact** between the solid and the surface: a smaller area gives a larger pressure.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define density. *[2 marks]*

(ii) State and explain how the density of the air in a room changes when the temperature of the room increases. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Density** is the **mass per unit volume** of a substance: $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V}$. Its SI unit is $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$.

(ii) The density of the air **decreases**.

**Explanation:** when the air is heated its molecules move faster and farther apart, so the air **expands**. The volume of the room is fixed, so part of the expanded air escapes through the openings (windows, doors, gaps), and the **mass of air in the room becomes smaller** while the volume stays the same. With $\rho = m/V$ and $m$ decreasing, the density falls. (For a given mass of air that is free to expand, the volume increases at constant mass, which also lowers the density.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State Ohm's law. *[2 marks]*

A student carried out an experiment to show how the potential difference, V, across the ends of a wire varies with the current, I, flowing through the wire and obtained the following data.

| V/V | 0 | 2.0 | 4.2 | 6.4 | 8.4 | 11.4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I/A | 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 |

(ii) Plot a graph of V (y-axis) against I (x-axis). *[6 marks]*

(iii) Determine the gradient of your graph. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Ohm's law:** the **current through a metallic conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends**, provided its temperature and other physical conditions remain constant ($V = IR$).

(ii) **Graph to plot (described).** Axes: current $I$/A on the x-axis (scale $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ to $1\,\mathrm{A}$, from 0 to 10) and potential difference $V$/V on the y-axis (scale $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ to $1\,\mathrm{V}$, from 0 to 12), both labelled with units. Plot the six points $(I, V)$: $(0, 0)$, $(2, 2.0)$, $(4, 4.2)$, $(6, 6.4)$, $(8, 8.4)$, $(10, 11.4)$. Draw the **best straight line through the origin**. The first five points lie almost exactly on a line; the last point $(10, 11.4)$ lies a little above it, and the line is drawn with points on both sides of it.

(iii) Take a large triangle on the line, for example between $(0, 0)$ and $(10, 10.9)$:

$$\text{gradient} = \dfrac{\Delta V}{\Delta I} = \dfrac{10.9 - 0}{10 - 0} \approx 1.1\,\Omega$$

The gradient is about **$1.1\,\Omega$** (accept $1.0$ to $1.15\,\Omega$; a best fit through the origin on all six points gives $1.09\,\Omega$). It is the **resistance $R$ of the wire**, and the straight line through the origin shows that the wire obeys Ohm's law.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define resistance. *[2 marks]*

(ii) State two factors that affect the resistance of a metallic conductor. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The **resistance** of a conductor is the **ratio of the potential difference across it to the current flowing through it**: $R = \dfrac{V}{I}$. Its unit is the ohm ($\Omega$), $1\,\Omega = 1\,\mathrm{V\,A^{-1}}$.

(ii) The resistance of a metallic conductor depends on (any two): its **length** (longer wire, larger resistance); its **cross-sectional area** (thicker wire, smaller resistance); the **material** it is made of (its resistivity); its **temperature** (resistance of a metal increases when it is hotter), as in $R = \dfrac{\rho L}{A}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define current. *[2 marks]*

(ii) A radio rated $1500\,W$ is connected to a $240\,V$ mains supply when in use. Calculate the current flowing through the device. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Current** is the **rate of flow of electric charge** past a point in a circuit: $I = \dfrac{Q}{t}$. Its unit is the ampere ($1\,\mathrm{A} = 1\,\mathrm{C\,s^{-1}}$).

(ii) Power $P = IV$, so

$$I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{1500\,\mathrm{W}}{240\,\mathrm{V}} = 6.25\,\mathrm{A}$$

The current through the radio is about **$6.3\,\mathrm{A}$** ($6.25\,\mathrm{A}$).
